user.title: GRIB Weather Overlay
user.description: Choose a GRIB data source and enter your API key.

data_description.notification_api_key: Optional: a separate KNMI **Notification Service** key (developer.dataplatform.knmi.nl → Notification Service) for instant push updates of new forecast runs. This is NOT your Open Data key: the broker refuses that with 'Not authorized'. Leave empty to rely on periodic polling — nothing else changes.

parameters.title: Choose parameters
parameters.description: Select which weather parameters should be kept up to date and made available to the map card.

error.invalid_auth: The API key was rejected by the source.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the source's API.

abort.already_configured: This source/dataset combination is already configured.

data.retain_runs: Number of forecast runs to keep cached
data.storage_apply_all: Use this folder for all sources

data_description.parameters: Which parameters of this dataset to download and show. A parameter you switch on appears after the current forecast run has been processed again (that starts right after saving).
data_description.notification_api_key: Optional: a separate KNMI **Notification Service** key (developer.dataplatform.knmi.nl → Notification Service) for instant push updates of new forecast runs. This is NOT your Open Data key: the broker refuses that with 'Not authorized'. Leave empty to rely on periodic polling — nothing else changes.
data_description.observations_api_key: Optional: a KNMI Open Data key with access to the '10-minute-in-situ-meteorological-observations' dataset, used to download station observations. Your HARMONIE key is often not authorised for it (KNMI returns 403). Leave empty to reuse the HARMONIE key.
data_description.alias: Optional short name shown as this source's compact label in the comparison and meteogram views, e.g. `KNMI NL`. Leave empty to derive it automatically from the source (same-source entries are disambiguated automatically).
data_description.storage_path: Where the GRIB working files are kept (the GRIB records being decoded and the rendered cache). Pick a network storage you added under Settings → System → Storage (a NAS): the files then go to a `grib_overlay` folder on it, which spares the local SSD the writes and is never part of a backup. Or type a path, or leave empty for the default `/var/tmp/grib_overlay`: outside every backup, and emptied when Home Assistant is updated (the runs are then simply downloaded again). Never use a folder inside `/config` (or `/share` / `/media` if your backups include them). When the folder changes, the cache at the old place is removed and the current run is downloaded again.
data_description.storage_apply_all: Give every GRIB Weather Overlay source the folder above, not just this one.
data_description.color_scales: One parameter per line, e.g. `wind_10m: 0:#2c7fb8, 8:#7fcdbb, 12:#ffffb2, 16:#fd8d3c, 24:#bd0026`. Values are in the parameter's own unit (m/s, °C, hPa, mm, m). Your parameters: {parameters}. Leave empty to use the built-in colours. Changing this re-renders the current run.

error.storage_not_writable: This folder cannot be used: it could not be created or is not writable. Check that the network storage is connected under Settings → System → Storage.
